observed_result.summary: Lock continuity: fresh authentications continue through desktop and vault lock without the original vault staying unlocked; the lock-revokes alternative behaves differently and is disclosed once (R-UX-03); the process-restart re-issue row. macOS is mechanism evidence (debug build, test store); Windows is the release-profile product DPAPI row.

limitations: macOS lock rows are a debug build on the test store: mechanism evidence, never the macOS lock_continuity claim (B3, F03).

Blocked: the macOS login-keychain product row (B3), the Linux desktop row (B11), the 1Password vault row (B1) and the Windows system-agent vault row (B4); the lock-procedure checks (a03_*) are native steps apart from the exit build window (m03-plan §4.4).

Lock-revokes grant R (ADR-0008 D7, §17.42; the orchestrator's rulings on I-11 and I-12): a session_locked revocation is local and immediate. R's tombstone commits with its move to revoking, and every fresh login of R through Heimdall's endpoint is refused from then on (the attribution check: 0 of R's key IDs accepted after the revocation). The managed adapter's obligation then becomes a bounded_by_expiry obligation for R's pair (the world's enrollment carries no clock measurement, so unmeasured); once R's certificate's valid_before has passed on safe time the supervisor moves R to revoked, its record kept with the obligation nominally_expired (§17.15). R never returns to active. In this run R's policy window, and so its certificate's validity, is 600 s (ruling I-12), so its residual passes inside the lock and the post-unlock check reads revoked.

The macOS lock row ran at E8 7b75c4c1 and binds to the exit build E9 2b79aac1 (the E5-to-E9 precedent): E8..E9 is cfg(windows) product code, a macro whose expansion elsewhere is the command itself, and Windows tests, and the lock run's binaries (heimdall, e2e_exit_m03, integration_session_lock) built at E8 and at E9 in one scratch worktree with lock-macos.sh's commands are identical in all 17 sections, their non-debug symbols and LC_UUID; only the debug map's per-build object names differ, exactly as between two builds of E9 (macos-lock/e8-e9-identity/).

Status discipline (m03-plan §3, M01 rule E15): verified rows mean the required tests ran and passed on that platform in this run; not an independent review of the units. The lowest-row rule applies: a blocked owner-input row (m03-plan §7, B1-B13) keeps its record blocked, and no claim is widened to cover it.

Debug test builds on the test store are mechanism evidence only: only a release-profile run on a product store kind can carry a custody claim (ADR-0008 D12 item 3, F03); in M03 that is the Windows DPAPI row alone. The macOS lock_continuity claim stays not_verified (B3).

Linux and Windows binaries are cross-built on the macOS host with zig and run natively on the hosts (Windows: built and run natively on the PC); tests that read the repository at its compile-time path run on the build host only (case-index.json build_host_paths): a platform-neutral one counts as run elsewhere, any other keeps its row in_progress (harness gap).
The Docker cases (#[ignore = "docker: …"]) run on the macOS build host only (HM_DOCKER_TESTS=1 after up.sh): the devbox has no Docker (B8) and the Windows PC runs the fixture sshd in WSL scratch.
Proptest regression files resolve at compile-time source paths: persisted regression seeds replay on macOS only; the fixed default seeds run everywhere.

Every fixture is disposable: per-run keys, the loopback fixture sshd, disposable ssh-agents with a scratch HOME, scratch configuration, scratch and disposable file keychains, a disposable WSL distribution; the owners' keys, agents, keychains, ~/.ssh and Git configuration are never test material (m03-plan §0.2).
